model: General insurer FCFE at cost of equity on insurance revenue (engine route)

inputs.base_revenue_basis: FY2025 IFRS 17 insurance revenue, continuing operations (US Motor discontinued; FY2024 re-presented to 4,553.4 so FY2025 growth is +9.4%, not +4.3% against the as-reported 4,776.2 in the CSV)
inputs.share_count_basis: FY2025 weighted-average diluted 307,190,136 (ADM.L_Annual_FY2025.txt:18920); 306,304,680 in issue at 31 Dec 2025 with ~5m held by the employee benefit trust. Held FLAT: the employee share-scheme cost is fully expensed via sbc_pct_path, and the H1 2026 GBP45m buyback / EBT market purchases are the cash mechanism keeping the count flat (value-neutral per house rule).
inputs.net_debt_note: Net debt held at ZERO by the financials convention. The 1,819.9 total_debt in the CSV is predominantly funding for the Admiral Money loan book (gross loans GBP1.88bn at Jun-26) plus GBP250m-equivalent subordinated notes and GBP73.6m lease liabilities; it is operating funding of a lending business already reflected in net interest income, not a claim on the FCFE stream. Cash 301.1 sits inside the regulated insurance entities against policyholder liabilities (solvency ratio 193% at Dec-25, 190% at Jun-26 post-dividend-and-buyback) and is not surplus to shareholders.
inputs.last_fcf_basis: FY2025 distributable FCFE = continuing profit after tax 745.3 less ~10% capital retention (74.5) consistent with management's ~90% total payout guidance (65% normal dividend + surplus via buyback). The owner-FCF identity (reported_fcf - sbc - interest_income) is NOT applicable on this route: an insurer's statutory OCF/FCF is float-investment timing noise.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Statutory OCF 436.5 less capex 74.3 (FY2025); recorded for audit only, not used.
inputs.interest_income_note: Investment income (GBP215.5m FY2025) is an operating return on the insurance float and stays inside the stream; nothing is stripped because no cash pile is added to the bridge.
inputs.sbc_source: ADM.L_Metrics.csv StockBasedComp (cash-flow add-back for employee free share / DFSS schemes): FY2025 75.0, FY2024 67.8, FY2023 63.3. EquityAwardTaxes 0 every year (awards satisfied with EBT market purchases, GBP35.3m in FY2025).
inputs.buyback_note: Zero share repurchases in every cash-flow statement FY2018-FY2025. H1 2026 declared the first-ever GBP45m buyback (new policy: 65% normal dividend + surplus returned via buyback rather than special dividend from the 2026 interim onward); it had not started by the 6 Aug 2026 release, so recorded as 0 (authorized is not spent).
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in GBP millions; LSE quote in pence (GBp). 1 GBP = 100 GBp by definition, no market rate involved, so the rate cannot go stale. Parity check not applicable (no dual listing; the US OTC line AMIGY is an illiquid ADR). Per-share values are computed in GBP and multiplied by 100 to pence so the canonical intrinsic_value / weighted_iv are directly comparable to current_price.
inputs.price_note: Yahoo Finance chart API regular close (LSE closes 16:30 BST = 15:30Z). Price is ex the 70.5p interim dividend (ex-date 3 Sep 2026, paid 2 Oct 2026). 52-week range 2624-4128.
inputs.balance_sheet_note: The H1 2026 extraction is the 114-line results announcement only (no balance sheet or share-count note), so equity 1,443.3 and diluted shares 307.2m are the 31 Dec 2025 figures. Equity at 30 Jun 2026 is estimated ~GBP1.4bn (H1 NPAT ~330m less 715m final+interim dividends paid... see insurer_anchors). Refresh both when the full interim report is extracted.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity 9.0% built in GBP: UK 10-year gilt ~4.5% (2026) + equity beta ~0.9 x 5.0% ERP = 9.0%. No debt in the discount rate because the stream is post-financing FCFE (Admiral Money funding cost and subordinated-note coupons are already inside PBT). Same rate in all three scenarios: cyclicality and credit risk are charged in the driver paths, not stacked on the discount rate (risk charged once). Same 9.0% as IAG.AX (AUD) for comparability across the insurer set.
inputs.lease_treatment: Leases are inside the stream: IFRS 16 depreciation and interest on GBP73.6m of lease liabilities are already expensed in PBT, and lease liabilities are excluded from the (zero) net debt. One treatment, consistent with net_debt = 0.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI is immaterial (GBP0.3m FY2025 loss attributable to NCI); flows are taken as attributable to Admiral shareholders with no bridge deduction.
inputs.notes: MODEL: FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine (precedent: IAG.AX 'NEP not BVPS', GL, PRU). The dcf-methods routing table defaults insurers to BVPS-compounding x exit P/B, overridden because Admiral does NOT compound book: ROE 29-57% with a ~90% payout (dividends paid 332.7m FY2018 -> 715.4m FY2025) leaves equity at GBP0.76-1.44bn against a ~GBP11bn market cap (P/B ~7.6x), so an exit P/B multiple would carry the entire valuation. The value is the earnings stream. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = IFRS 17 insurance revenue (continuing); ebitda_margin_path = pre-SBC profit-before-tax margin on insurance revenue (FY2025: (957.9 + 75.0) / 4,979.3 = 20.7%); sbc_pct_path = employee share-scheme charge (1.5%), kept explicit so the house/street band shows what the free-share scheme costs owners; da_pct_path and lease_cost_pct_path = 0 because depreciation (79.0) is already inside PBT and roughly equals capex (74.3); capex_pct_path is REPURPOSED as earnings retention (~10% of post-tax profit, ~1.5% of revenue) that funds SCR growth and keeps solvency near 190%; wc_capture_pct = 0; cash_tax_rate_path 23% (FY2025 effective 22.2% on 957.9; UK statutory 25% diluted by European results; cash tax paid 192.1 = 20%). CYCLE: FY2025 is a near-peak year for UK motor (group combined ratio 80.1% vs 76.9% in FY2024, loss ratio rising 55.3% -> 59.2%, UK written premiums -3%, c.GBP30m Ogden tailwind). H1 2026 PBT -18%, EPS -18%, insurance revenue -1%, ROE 45% vs 57%. Management: market prices plateaued end-2025, Admiral raised motor rates in early 2026 ahead of the market; customer growth continues (+5% risks to 12.03m); Flock (commercial motor insurtech) acquired Q2 2026. Admiral Money loans +39% YoY to GBP1.88bn is the fastest-growing balance-sheet exposure and is the main non-cycle bear axis.

insurer_anchors.fy2021_note: FY2021 net income 997.9 includes the GBP404.4m gain on the sale of the Comparison business (Penguin Portals); continuing NPAT was 583.3. Not a base for anything.
insurer_anchors.fy2024_note: FY2024 UK Motor result included a GBP100m Ogden discount-rate gain; FY2025 c.GBP30m. Both inside the ebitda_margin anchors and the reason FY0 margin is treated as above mid-cycle.

historical_growth.fcf_cagr_basis: Continuing profit after tax as the FCFE proxy (FY2020 502.0, FY2022 286.5, FY2025 745.3); statutory FCF is float-timing noise and was not used
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: medium-term insurance-revenue growth = ~5%/yr customer growth (risks 6.51m FY2018 -> 12.03m H1 2026, 8.5% CAGR, slowing) with price roughly flat through the cycle; corroborated by equity 5yr CAGR 5.3% and EPS 5yr CAGR 6.5%, both measured peak-to-peak (FY2020 and FY2025 were both strong years)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 5.3% vs revenue 5yr CAGR 17.1%: >30% divergence. Expected for Admiral: ~90% of earnings are distributed so book does not compound, and 2023-25 revenue growth was the UK motor hard-market repricing (insurance revenue +18%/+11%/+9% while customer numbers grew 5-13%). Neither CAGR is a forward growth rate; the driver paths are set from the cycle, not the CAGRs.
historical_growth.notes: 3-year CAGRs are measured from the FY2022 trough (inflation shock, PBT 361.2, EPS 95.4p) and are meaningless as trend. Revenue series has two definitional breaks: pre-FY2022 the CSV revenue is pre-IFRS 17 total revenue; FY2024 is as-reported including US Motor (4,776.2) while FY2025 compares against re-presented 4,553.4.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 -1.5%: H1 insurance revenue -1% with written premiums having fallen through 2025 (earned revenue lags written by ~6 months), partly offset by +5% risks and Flock. FY2027-29 +4-5% as early-2026 rate rises earn through and customers compound ~5%; fades to 2.5% by year 10.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-SBC PBT margin on insurance revenue: FY2025 20.7% (near-peak, incl. c.GBP30m Ogden). FY2026 18.0% implies PBT ~GBP810m, -15% (H1 was -18% vs the H1 2025 peak half). Mid-cycle 17.0% (PBT margin 15.5%, combined ratio ~83%) sits between the FY2023 trough (14.5%) and FY2025 peak (20.7%) and reflects Admiral's structural expense-ratio edge (20.9% vs UK market high-20s%) persisting.
base.capex_rationale: Capital retention ~1.5% of revenue = ~10% of post-tax profit, the complement of the ~90% payout guided (65% normal dividend + surplus via buyback). Equivalent to growing own funds ~GBP75m/yr against an SCR growing ~5%.
base.terminal_rationale: Gordon at 9.0%/2.5% = 15.8x FCFE; cap 16x (a mature best-in-class personal-lines insurer; Admiral's own 10-year P/E range is ~12-20x). Gordon binds.

bull.growth_rationale: Admiral repeats its 2018 and 2023-24 pattern of taking share when it moves on price ahead of the market: UK Motor vehicles grow 6-8%, UK Household/Travel/Pet keep compounding ~20% off a small base, Europe stays profitable, Flock scales in commercial motor.
bull.margin_rationale: Mild soft market in 2026 (margin 19%) then a sustained ~18.5% pre-SBC PBT margin: combined ratio stays low-80s as claims inflation keeps falling, co-insurer profit commissions normalise higher, investment income holds ~4% yield, Admiral Money reaches ~GBP50m PBT.
bull.capex_rationale: Slightly higher retention (1.75%) because faster premium growth needs more SCR.
bull.narrative: Price-led share gain, soft patch short

bear.growth_rationale: The 2026 UK motor price recovery is delayed (the Group's own ORSA stress), Admiral holds rate and loses volume: insurance revenue -3% then flat, recovering only to ~3% nominal growth.
bear.margin_rationale: Prolonged soft market: combined ratio drifts to high-80s (pre-SBC PBT margin 13.5-14% in FY2027-28, i.e. PBT ~GBP600m, a FY2023-like level), compounded by higher Admiral Money impairments on a GBP1.9bn book grown 39% in a year, FCA pricing/claims-handling intervention, and continued European and Flock drag. Mature margin 15% (PBT margin 13.5%).
bear.capex_rationale: Lower retention (1.0%) because slower growth needs less new SCR; payout stays ~90% as guided.
bear.terminal_rationale: Cap 14x for a business shown to be more cyclical than the market assumes.

scenario_narratives.base: UK motor follows a normal cycle. FY2025 was close to the top (combined ratio 80%, written premiums already falling as prices reduced) and H1 2026 confirmed the turn (PBT -18%, insurance revenue -1%, dividend -39% on the new 65%-payout policy). Admiral raised rates in early 2026 ahead of the market; written premiums bottom in 2026 and earned revenue grows 4-5% from 2027 as pricing and 5%/yr customer growth earn through. Pre-SBC PBT margin settles at 17% of insurance revenue (PBT margin 15.5%, between the FY2023 trough and FY2025 peak), with the structural expense-ratio advantage, quota-share profit commissions and ~4% investment yields intact. About 90% of profit is distributed (65% normal dividend plus buybacks), 10% retained to keep solvency near 190%. Discounted at a 9% GBP cost of equity, Gordon at 2.5% binds below the 16x cap.
scenario_narratives.bull: Admiral does what it did in 2018 and 2023-24: having moved on price before the market, it takes share as competitors reprice, growing UK vehicles 6-8% and insurance revenue 6-7% for three years. UK Household, Travel and Pet keep compounding ~20% off a small base, Europe stays profitable after the 2025 turnaround, Flock scales Admiral into commercial motor, and Admiral Money reaches ~GBP50m PBT without a credit event. Claims inflation keeps easing so the combined ratio holds in the low-80s and the pre-SBC PBT margin stays ~18.5%. Terminal growth 3%; the 16x cap binds.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 2026 UK motor price recovery is delayed (the stress the Group itself models in its ORSA) and Admiral, holding rate, sheds volume: insurance revenue -3% then flat. A prolonged soft market pushes the combined ratio to the high-80s and PBT to a FY2023-like ~GBP600m in FY2027-28. Admiral Money, having grown gross loans 39% in a year to GBP1.9bn, takes elevated consumer-credit impairments; FCA pricing and claims-handling intervention compresses UK personal-lines margins; Europe and Flock remain small drags. Mature pre-SBC PBT margin 15%, terminal growth 2%, cap 14x. Dividends fall with profits under the 65% payout policy; buybacks are the first lever cut.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25% because the soft-cycle downside is live, not hypothetical (H1 2026 PBT -18%, written premiums down through 2025, the Group's own ORSA names a delayed 2026 price recovery as its first stress) and Admiral Money's 39% loan growth adds a consumer-credit axis the business did not have at the last trough. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs the price-led share gain, continued low claims inflation and a clean Admiral Money book to all hold simultaneously. Base 50%: Admiral has emerged from every prior soft market with share gains and 50%+ ROE, so the central case is a normal cycle, not a broken one.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Admiral is valued as an earnings stream, not a book. A capital-light, quota-share-reinsured personal-lines insurer that earns 45-57% ROE and distributes ~90% of it has no compounding book to multiply; its worth is the probability-weighted present value of the distributable profit the UK motor cycle lets it earn, discounted at a 9% GBP cost of equity. FY2025 is treated as near the top of that cycle (combined ratio 80%, Ogden tailwind, written premiums already shrinking) and H1 2026 as the turn, so year one steps down and the mid-cycle margin is set below FY2025 rather than extrapolated from it. The house basis expenses the GBP75m/yr employee free-share scheme; the street basis treats it as non-cash, and the gap between the two is what the price is paying for that scheme.
key_risks_to_valuation: UK motor pricing cycle: a delayed or shallow 2026 price recovery (the Group's own primary ORSA stress) pushes FY2027-28 towards the bear path
Admiral Money: gross loans +39% YoY to GBP1.88bn; a UK consumer-credit downturn would hit a book that has not been through a recession at this size
Claims inflation re-accelerating (repair costs, bodily injury, Ogden rate review) ahead of repricing
FCA intervention on pricing practices, premium finance or claims handling compressing UK personal-lines margins
Reinsurance/co-insurance terms: Admiral retains ~40-50% of UK motor risk and earns profit commission on the rest; harder quota-share terms reduce the structural margin edge
Investment income: the ~4% portfolio yield is ~GBP215m of FY2025 profit and falls with gilt yields
Capital policy: the new 65% normal dividend + buyback framework is untested; solvency 190% leaves buffer but a sustained soft market cuts distributions one-for-one
Europe (Italy/France/Spain) and the Flock commercial-motor acquisition: small today but have been loss-making before
Anchors: equity and diluted share count are 31 Dec 2025 vintage (the H1 2026 extraction is the announcement only) and should be refreshed when the full interim report is extracted
